questions.question: Motorcyclists must wear a helmet.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: In Illinois, wearing a helmet is not required by law. However, helmets greatly reduce the risk of fatal head injuries and are strongly recommended.

questions.question: In Illinois, which is allowed on a motorcycle?

options.text: A modified muffler that makes it louder
Handlebars higher than the rider's head
A blue license plate light
A seat designed for two people

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat designed for two people
questions.explanation: Illinois requires motorcycles to have a white license plate light. You cannot modify the muffler to be louder. Handlebars must not be higher than the rider's head. Passengers can only ride if the motorcycle and seat are designed for two people.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen
Help you avoid surface hazards
Provide you with an escape route
Invite other drivers to share your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane
questions.explanation: Good lane positioning keeps you out of blind spots, helps you see and be seen, helps you avoid hazards, and gives you an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know they see you
Is not worth the effort
Does not mean they will yield to you
Guarantees they will yield to you

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not register that they are there.

questions.question: To work properly, a face shield should NOT:

options.text: Be free of scratches
Allow clear views to both sides
Be airtight
Fasten securely

questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, allow clear side views, fasten securely, and let air pass through. An airtight face shield causes fogging and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: In a group ride, less experienced riders should be:

options.text: In the front
Just behind the lead rider
In the rear

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This allows more experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers
Always ride with your headlight on
Wave your arms
Ride closely behind other vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on
questions.explanation: To be more visible at intersections, ride with your headlight on and position yourself where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Never assume eye contact means a driver sees you.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while riding in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting it
Switch lanes as quickly as possible
Stay in your lane
Flash your lights to scare the animal away

questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal, but stay in your lane when in traffic. Swerving into other lanes can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible
Hold onto the seat
Put their feet on the muffler
Get on after you start the engine

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after you start the engine
questions.explanation: Before riding with a passenger, give them complete safety instructions. Have them board after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as comfortable and firmly hold your waist or belt. Keep their feet on the footrests at all times.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane
Pull off the road until the rain stops
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
Increase your speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: Avoid riding in the center of the lane when it is wet. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track usually works best, but this depends on traffic conditions.

questions.question: To be visible in a driver's rearview mirror, where should you position your vehicle?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
In the left part of your lane.
In the right part of your lane.
In a weaving pattern across the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of your lane behind the other vehicle. This places you directly in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: A person convicted of DUI (driving under the influence) can receive all of the following penalties, except:

options.text: License suspension.
Installation of a breath-alcohol device in their vehicle.
A fine.
A warning.

questions.explanation: DUI penalties in Illinois include license suspension, installation of a breath-alcohol device, large fines, and community service. A simple warning is not a penalty for DUI.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does the body process per hour?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. The time to lower blood alcohol content varies by person. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should travel:

options.text: More slowly than during the day with similar conditions.
At the same speed as during the day with similar conditions.
Faster than during the day with similar conditions.
On the road shoulder so others can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than during the day with similar conditions.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than you would during the day under the same weather and traffic conditions. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Slower speeds help you avoid hazards.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Perform braking and swerving as separate actions. Do not brake while swerving because this can cause your motorcycle to tip over.
